text:
maria: Heads up — I found a plaintext service key in a staging ConfigMap created by a partner import job. Not in prod, but likely used by their CI job.
aj: thanks, can you paste the path/resource?
maria: namespace=partner-staging, configmap=partner-ingest-config, key=GCP_SA_KEY (base64 blob). Saw it in `kubectl get cm -n partner-staging partner-ingest-config -o yaml` dump.
kevin: ack. Is this the long-lived JSON key or a short-lived token?
maria: looks like a JSON SA key (full private_key). Dates look old.
sophie: ok prioritize rotation. Who can delete the key from GCP and revoke it?
aj: I can run the revoke once we confirm the SA id. Maria, can you paste the `client_email` from the JSON (no private key content)?
maria: client_email: partner-ingest@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
kevin: that SA matches the partner onboarding account. Action plan: 1) revoke the current key in GCP 2) delete the key material from the ConfigMap 3) rotate to an ephemeral workload identity token or avoid embedding SA keys in k8s 4) add audit-only policy and RBAC cleanup.
aj: I'll delete the key now. Command: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=partner-ingest@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json | jq '.[].name'` then `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_NAME --iam-account=...`
ryan-oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-348 (severity: medium). Pager duty alerted.
sophie: Maria, after AJ deletes the key, can you patch the ConfigMap to remove the field and push a replacement secret referencing `workload-identity`? Minimal downtime.
maria: on it — will prepare a patch. Also adding `kubectl annotate` to mark `secrets/rotated-by=eng-security`.
kevin: we should wrap up with Vault rewrap for any backups: check backups for any persisted ciphertext. Also ensure KMS wrapping keys haven't been exported.
aj: Revoke done. GCP response: "Key deleted." Took 2 mins.
maria: patched configmap to remove key, applied a Kubernetes `Secret` referencing the new short-lived token from the partner's CI job. Paste: `kubectl patch cm partner-ingest-config -n partner-staging --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/data/GCP_SA_KEY"}]'`
sophie: great. Next: schedule a short postmortem and RBAC hardening. We should: - require CI jobs to use Workload Identity - add an admission controller policy to block base64-encoded JSON in ConfigMaps/Secrets - enable audit log alerting on `iam.serviceAccounts.keys.create` and `delete` - run a one-off search for similar patterns across clusters.
kevin: I'll file a ticket for the admission controller and add an eval job to run the cluster-wide grep for `client_email` patterns.
sec-eng-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/credential-leak-cleanup. Recommended checklist: rotate, revoke, remove, audit, retro.
aj: quick note — partner's repo has a self-run script that writes the key. We'll ask partner to remove it and switch to Workload Identity. Sophie, can you own partner comms?
sophie: yes, will take lead and copy eng-security. Drafting message now.
maria: logging: enabled k8s audit forwarder for partner namespace and flagged all accesses in the last 30 days. Exporting log slice to GCS for SRE/forensics.
kevin: Thanks. Closing steps: 1) confirm partner removed key from their repo 2) admission controller policy PR 3) postmortem + RCA 4) update onboarding docs to forbid static SA keys.
aj: marking done for key revoke and CM patch. Will update INC-2026-348.
sophie: will send partner note and schedule a 30-min sync.
maria: filing the postmortem doc and adding a short remediation checklist.
kevin: nice work team. :thumbsup:
